saml.description: SAML login flows may omit the role parameter only when the auth mount has a default_role configured.
saml.note: A missing explicit role is not a bug if default_role is configured; it is by-design role selection.

saml.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias name and thereby gain access to that alias's privileges.
saml.note: Collision-like outcomes involving intentionally reused aliases may be by design of Vault identity aliasing, not a parser confusion bug.

saml.description: When group_policy_application_mode is set to 'any', identity group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy.
saml.note: Cross-namespace group-derived policy reach is expected in this mode and should not be flagged as privilege escalation.

saml.constraint: SAML config trust source is mutually exclusive: configure_jwt_validation MUST set either idp_metadata_url OR the explicit trio idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. Do not send idp_metadata_url together with explicit IdP URL/entity/cert fields, or setup is invalid.

For I1 SAML signature-integrity tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST explicitly enable validate_assertion_signature=true. If only validate_response_signature is enabled, Vault is only configured to validate at least the response signature, which can make unsigned-assertion or assertion-level signature tests ambiguous.

For spurious-signature and unsigned-assertion tests, configure_jwt_validation SHOULD enable both validate_response_signature=true and validate_assertion_signature=true to test whether Vault verifies the exact assertion it consumes rather than merely detecting some valid signature in the envelope.

For I1 issuer-mismatch tests, when not using metadata, configure_jwt_validation MUST set idp_entity_id to the trusted IdP entity ID. The attack SAML assertion must then carry a different Issuer. Without a configured trusted entity ID, issuer-validation setup is incomplete.

For I5 audience tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST set sp_entity_id (entity_id) to the SP entity ID expected in SAML AudienceRestriction. Use that exact value as the control audience and a different value for wrong-audience attacks.

saml_start_login and saml_exchange_for_token are session-bound by client_challenge/client_verifier and token_poll_id. For valid I3 flow-coherence tests, do not mix token_poll_id or verifier values across sessions; a mismatch is expected rejection, not a vulnerability.

saml_start_login requires acs_url to be one of the configured acs_urls. The fuzzer MUST use an ACS URL from configure_jwt_validation.acs_urls exactly; otherwise login failure is a setup error, not a security finding.

If configure_jwt_validation.default_role is unset, saml_start_login MUST provide role explicitly. Omitting role without a configured default_role causes expected login failure and invalidates security conclusions.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only. If bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' is wildcard. For I4 multi-identity scenarios requiring multiple different subjects to pass the same role, either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern; never set bound_subjects='*' while using string mode, because only the literal '*' will match.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type. If bound_attributes_type=string (default), values are exact string matches only; if glob, '*' wildcards are honored. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, exact-match attribute constraints that would exclude alternate identities MUST be omitted rather than set to wildcard-looking literals under string mode.

bound_attributes accepted values are documented as a single string or comma-separated list of strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests, Vault SAML docs do not document numeric/boolean attribute value handling. The fuzzer SHOULD test type coercion explicitly by binding a numeric-looking string value and sending alternate typed representations if the SAML generator supports them; otherwise treat non-string attribute values as unspecified behavior, not a confirmed bypass.
token_num_uses has sentinel semantics: value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Never interpret 0 as 'deny all' or 'single use'.
saml.source: auth/saml role read response token fields

saml.constraint: token_ttl, token_max_ttl, token_explicit_max_ttl, and token_period use sentinel semantics in Vault token fields: value 0 means use system/mount/default behavior or no explicit limit, not literal immediate expiry. Never assume 0 disables the underlying token or makes it expired.
saml.source: auth/saml role read response token fields

saml.constraint: token_num_uses limits every API call made with the issued session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and a protected-resource read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-authenticated verification calls are present.
saml.source: auth/saml role token fields and fuzzer execution context

saml.constraint: For I2 SAML replay tests, prefer replaying the exact same SAMLResponse through saml_login/callback. Do not regenerate a fresh assertion between attempts, or the test stops being an assertion-ID / OneTimeUse replay test.

For I2 freshness tests on issued Vault tokens versus upstream SAML assertions, include a control login with a valid SAMLResponse alongside the replay/expired/invalid attack. Without a control, callback or token exchange failure may reflect broken setup rather than freshness enforcement.

External group membership for SAML group mapping should be modeled via groups_attribute on the role plus identity group aliases. Do not rely on manually setting member_entity_ids on an external-style mapping to simulate upstream SAML groups; that tests Vault identity internals, not SAML group alias resolution.
saml.source: identity/group and identity/group-alias APIs plus auth/saml role groups_attribute

saml.constraint: Group alias creation requires the auth mount accessor, not the mount path. The fuzzer MUST call get_mount_accessor and use the returned accessor in create_group_alias; sending the mount path will not create a valid alias mapping.

Vault identity alias cardinality matters: alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias and share privileges. When constructing I4 collision tests, treat same alias name on the same mount accessor as a potentially shared identity by design of the identity system, not necessarily a parser bug in SAML itself.
verify_read_secret on KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment. Using /{engine}/{path} instead of /{engine}/data/{path} yields wrong-endpoint failures unrelated to authorization.

KV v2 list capability is on /metadata/, not /data/. If a policy is intended to permit listing during setup or verification, grant list on /{engine}/metadata/* separately; lack of metadata-list permission is expected behavior, not an authorization-binding bug.

KV v2 CAS and deletion sentinels matter: options.cas=0 means create-only if the key does not yet exist, not 'disable CAS'. Engine config max_versions=0 means keep the default 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no scheduled deletion, not immediate deletion.

For I3 config-change sequences, new SAML logins are evaluated against the current auth mount and role configuration by design. A valid coherence test must show that a post-change login with the old assumptions is rejected or changed consistently; do not flag the mere fact that admin config changes affect subsequent logins.

MFA login enforcement creation requires at least one scoping field among auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids, or identity_entity_ids. For SAML MFA-bypass tests, scope enforcement to the SAML mount accessor or auth_method_types including the relevant method; otherwise setup is invalid.

For SAML MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, compare a baseline login path that triggers MFA with a SAML login for the same principal under the same enforcement scope. If the enforcement is not scoped to the SAML mount/accessor or entity/group, absence of MFA on SAML is expected setup behavior, not a bypass.

Group policy application mode can change cross-namespace policy inheritance. In Enterprise environments, if /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', group policies may apply across namespace boundaries by design. I5 group-policy escalation tests must account for this global mode before flagging cross-namespace policy reach as a bug.
